title: Saying sorry and fixing things
examples: What should I say when I accidentally knock over my friend's tower?
If I hurt someone's feelings, how do I make it better?
Can you give me an example of fixing a broken toy?

explain.say: Everyone makes mistakes. When you hurt someone or break something, you can say sorry.
Say what happened. Then say sorry. For example, I bumped your tower. I am sorry.

draw.text: I bumped your tower. I am sorry.

explain.say: Next, help to fix it. You can help build the tower again.
Look at your friend’s face. Think about how they feel. This is called empathy.

draw.text: Empathy: thinking about how someone else feels.

explain.say: Sometimes you need to fix a feeling. Say sorry and ask how you can help. Ask before you give a hug.

faq.q: What if I don't know how to fix it?
faq.a: It is okay if you do not know how to fix it right away. You can ask a grown-up for help to find a solution together.
asks: What do I do if I break something?
Who can help me fix it?

faq.a: No, saying sorry is just the start. You must also show you are trying to fix the problem or the feeling.
asks: Do I have to do something after I say sorry?

faq.a: You show empathy by noticing how someone looks or sounds. You might ask them, 'Are you okay?'
asks: How do I know if someone is sad?

faq.q: Does fixing things always mean physical things?
faq.a: No. Sometimes you fix a feeling. You can listen, share, or offer a hug if your friend wants one.

faq.q: What if my friend gets cross with me?
faq.a: If your friend is cross, stay calm. You can say, I see you are upset. Then listen to them.
asks: What to do when a friend is angry?

facts: Saying sorry is an important part of being a good friend.
Repairing something can mean fixing a toy or fixing a friendship.
Empathy means understanding how someone else feels.
After saying sorry, it is helpful to ask what you can do to help.

quiz.say: You step on Aoife’s drawing by accident. Tap what to do first.
quiz.why: Saying sorry shows Aoife you know what happened. Then you can help fix it.

wrong.0: Running away leaves Aoife upset and on her own.
wrong.2: Blaming Aoife is unfair, because the step was yours.

quiz.say: Sam’s ball is in a puddle. Sam is crying. Tap kind words.
quiz.show: ⚽ 💧 Sam’s ball is in a puddle.

options.show: You look sad. Can I help?
options.say: You look sad. Can I help?

quiz.why: Saying what you see shows you care. Offering help is kind.

wrong.0: Crying is okay, so it is kinder to ask how you can help.
wrong.1: Calling it silly can make Sam feel worse.

quiz.say: You break Kofi’s crayon. He is upset. Tap what to do.

options.show: Say sorry and ask how to help.
options.say: Say sorry and ask how to help.

options.show: Say it was an accident and walk off.
options.say: Say it was an accident and walk off.

quiz.why: Saying sorry and asking how to help fixes the problem and the feeling.

wrong.1: It was an accident, and Kofi still needs a sorry and some help.
wrong.2: Hiding the crayon leaves Kofi upset, so say sorry instead.
